title: Rav Giddel of Naresh
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Pesachim 107a: “Rav Huna said that Rav said, and so Rav Giddel of Naresh taught.” Hyman infers from the passage that he lived in the time of Rav Giddel without further designation. Hyman says that Yuchasin copied the Gemara improperly as “Rav Huna said: Giddel of Naresh taught,” and takes this to explain the words “I have not found it,” which he attributes to מה״ר.

notes.text: מה״ר remains literal and unidentified. Named Davidson Pesachim 107a fully writes Rav Huna reporting Rav and says Rav Giddel of Naresh likewise recited the teaching. Hyman’s inference and his report about a Yuchasin copy remain attributed; the unresolved מה״ר keeps the notice held.

Hyman’s printed page (vol. I, p. 304) has מה״ר. The consulted Yuchasin HaShalem (London and Edinburgh, 1857, p. 122) gives “Rav Huna said: Giddul of Naresh taught” and then gives Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak’s version with Giddul unqualified. Pesachim 107a first has Rav Huna reporting Rav and says Rav Giddel of Naresh likewise taught. The digital Warsaw text of Seder HaDorot, under Giddel of Naresh, gives the full opening and ends with “Rav Huna said (ל״מ).” This supplies a likely source for “I have not found it,” the quotation left unresolved in the preceding note. Hyman’s abbreviation remains unexpanded. The passage does not settle the relationship between the named and unqualified Giddel.
